implementerProof.how: Six of the seven things this round owed hold, and I drove each rather than reading the handoff for it: the no-kind refusal, the migration of all four old row shapes, both of the earlier controls re-run at this head, close_root on a waiting root, the prose, and the diff to my own test file. The seventh fails, and it is the one the round exists for: a kind listed in StatusRowKinds with no case in stillWanted does not fail the row loudly. It writes its status and returns nil, because stillWanted is reached only on an ISSUE_CHANGED retry while the first attempt branches on kind through an if-chain with no exhaustive default - the same shape as the statusKindOf default this round removed, one site over. The architect has accepted the finding and decided the fix; my probe becomes a permanent test.

failures.criterion: A kind listed in record.StatusRowKinds with no case in stillWanted fails the row loudly rather than borrowing another kind's rule - the guarantee this round's Kind field exists to provide.
failures.evidence: It does not fail: it writes its status and returns nil. In a scratch clone at 2e17816f I added a fifth kind the way a future one arrives - EscalationStatusRow = "escalation", added to StatusRowKinds so validateOutboxPayload accepts it - and gave it no case in stillWanted. Driving a row of it through the real executor (packages/daemon/internal/daemon, zz_listed_kind_probe_test.go, run with go test -run 'TestProbeAListedKindWithNoRule...'): 'validateOutboxPayload accepts it, because the kind is listed'; 'execute of a listed kind with no rule = <nil>'; 'statuses written by a kind with no rule = [testing]'. So the row ran, wrote, and took the ordinary path in silence. The mechanism is that stillWanted is reached only on an ISSUE_CHANGED retry. The path every row takes every time is the outbox's status executor, which branches on kind as an if-chain with no exhaustive default: 'if payload.Kind == record.HandOverStatusRow' (twice, plus dropHandover) and 'if payload.Kind == record.PersonHandoverStatusRow && !r.personHandoverStands(...)'. A kind nobody gave a case falls past every branch and is handled as an ordinary row - which is exactly what statusKindOf's 'default: return ordinaryStatusRow' did before this round. So the guarantee holds on the retry path alone, which is the rare path review round 6's defect lived in: a new kind would work in the common case and be judged by the wrong rule precisely when something else moved the issue underneath it. I did not write the fix. The architect has since decided it - every kind-dependent decision through one switch over Kind with a failing default, the first-attempt handling and the retry's rule becoming two methods of one per-kind value - and named this probe as the permanent test it becomes.

proof.criterion: A StatusWrite built with no Kind is refused before it reaches the outbox.
proof.surface: The record package's row construction and the daemon's real status executor over a fake Dispatch.
proof.observed: PASS, both cases of each. A row carrying no kind and a row of an unlisted kind are each refused at record.NewOutboxRow naming the kind ('unknown kind ""', 'unknown kind "escalation"'), and a stored row of that shape fails at execute with the same message and nothing written to Dispatch. The structural reason is worth recording because it is what makes the empty case work at all: StatusRowKind is a string, so its zero value is "" rather than the first constant. Had it been an iota int, an unkeyed literal would have been OrdinaryStatusRow and the refusal would never fire - the same hole one level down. TestEveryStatusRowKindHasAConstructorThatSetsIt holds each of the four kinds to a constructor that sets it and to validateOutboxPayload.
proof.negativeControl: The listed-kind probe recorded under failures is this item's control: it shows the refusal is specific to a kind the list does not name, and that a kind the list does name passes validation and reaches the executor.

notesForNextRound: The probe to keep is the listed-kind one, and the architect has said it becomes a permanent test: add a kind to record.StatusRowKinds, give it no case, and drive a row of it through the outbox's execute. It must fail naming the kind. Today it returns nil and writes the status, and the first-attempt path is where that happens - not stillWanted, which is only reached on an ISSUE_CHANGED retry.

When the fix lands, check both sites agree about which kinds exist, since that is the point of folding them into one per-kind value: a kind with a first-attempt method and no retry rule, or the reverse, is the same class again.

Push only the handoff while a CI run of the round's code is open. A code or test push starts a new run and cancels the one anybody asked about, which is how runs 41363374900 and 41364069009 ended cancelled last round.
Use CGO_ENABLED=1 for any -race run in this pod; without it the command exits 'go: -race requires cgo' and runs nothing, and a grep for DATA RACE then returns what a clean run returns.

Start NATS before the suite, and build a database legion_test owns (psql -tAc 'create database <name> owner legion_test') rather than pointing tests at the pod DSN's postgres database, where internal/daemon's migrations fail at 0001_init with 'permission denied for schema public'.
